questions.q: Which HTTP version made persistent connections the default behaviour?
questions.exp: HTTP/1.1 keeps connections open by default (keep-alive).

questions.q: In the URL https://www.example.com:8080/docs/index.html?id=5#top, which part is the query string?
questions.exp: The query string follows '?' and precedes '#'; here it is id=5.
The local var a is hoisted to the top of t but not yet assigned, so it logs undefined.

questions.q: A merge conflict in Git occurs when:
options: a branch name is longer than 40 characters
the same lines of a file were changed differently in the branches being merged
the remote repository has been deleted
questions.exp: Git cannot decide automatically between conflicting edits; the developer resolves them and commits.

questions.q:
What is the output?
console.log(0.1 + 0.2 === 0.3);
questions.exp: Floating-point representation makes 0.1 + 0.2 equal 0.30000000000000004, so the comparison is false.

questions.q: The PageRank algorithm used by the Google search engine was developed by:
questions.exp: PageRank was devised by Larry Page and Sergey Brin at Stanford.

questions.q: A form collects a user's password. Which method is more appropriate and why?
options: POST, because the data is not displayed in the URL
HEAD, because it has no body
questions.exp: POST sends data in the request body, so the password is not exposed in the URL or browser history (HTTPS is still needed for encryption).

questions.q:
What is the output?
console.log([1,2,3].map(x => x * 2).join("-"));
questions.exp: map doubles each element giving [2,4,6]; join with "-" gives 2-4-6.

questions.q: In a flex container with flex-direction: row, the property justify-content aligns the items along the:
questions.exp: justify-content works on the main axis, which is horizontal for row direction.

questions.q: Which attribute makes a hyperlink open the target page in a new browser tab?
questions.exp: target="_blank" opens the link in a new window or tab.

questions.q: Which service translates a domain name such as www.example.com into an IP address?
questions.exp: The Domain Name System resolves host names to IP addresses.
The dot is the concatenation operator, so the strings "5" and "3" join to give 53.

questions.q:
What is the output?
console.log(typeof [] + typeof {});
questions.exp: Both arrays and plain objects give typeof "object", so the strings concatenate to objectobject.

questions.q: Which HTML element groups related form controls and draws a box around them?
questions.exp: <fieldset> groups controls; <legend> supplies its caption.

questions.q: Which HTML5 element provides a scriptable region for drawing graphics using JavaScript?
questions.exp: <canvas> is the HTML5 drawing surface controlled through the Canvas API.

questions.q: Which sequence of Git commands correctly saves a local change and then shares it with a remote repository?
options: git commit, git add, git pull
git push, git add, git commit
git clone, git push, git commit
git add, git commit, git push
questions.exp: Changes are staged (git add), recorded in the local repository (git commit), then uploaded (git push).

questions.q: Given: li {color: red;} .item {color: green;} #first {color: blue;} and the element <li id="first" class="item">, what colour is the text?
questions.exp: An id selector has higher specificity than a class selector, which beats an element selector.

questions.q: According to the same-origin policy, two URLs have the same origin if they share the same:
questions.exp: Origin is defined as the combination of protocol (scheme), host name and port.

questions.q:
What is the output?
console.log(2 + "3" - 1);
questions.exp: 2 + "3" gives the string "23"; "23" - 1 coerces to number giving 22.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a web server software?
questions.exp: MySQL is a database management system, not a web server.
o.a[1] = 20 and o.a.length = 3, so 20 + 3 = 23.

questions.q: In PHP, which statement includes a file and stops the script with a fatal error if the file cannot be found?
questions.exp: require produces a fatal error on failure; include only gives a warning.

questions.q: The acronym LAMP, a common web development stack, stands for:
questions.exp: LAMP = Linux (OS), Apache (web server), MySQL (database), PHP (scripting); XAMPP/WAMP are variants.

questions.q: In a three-tier web application architecture, the web browser belongs to the:
questions.exp: The browser displays the user interface, which is the presentation tier.

questions.q: Which organisation develops and maintains the CSS specifications?
questions.exp: The World Wide Web Consortium (W3C) publishes the CSS standards; IETF handles HTTP RFCs.

questions.q: Which HTML5 attribute prefix allows custom data to be stored on any element?
questions.exp: data-* attributes (e.g. data-id) hold custom data accessible through the dataset property.

questions.q: Which DOM method adds a new node as the last child of a parent node?
questions.exp: appendChild() appends a node to the end of the parent's child list.

questions.q: Which event is fired when the mouse pointer moves onto an element?
questions.exp: onmouseover fires when the pointer enters an element.

questions.q: Which HTTP method is identical to GET except that the server returns no response body?
questions.exp: HEAD returns only the response headers.

questions.q: Which command installs the Express package using Node's package manager?
questions.exp: npm install <package> downloads the package into node_modules and records it in package.json.

questions.q: A group of radio buttons that share the same name attribute allows the user to select:
options: only one option in the group
questions.exp: Radio buttons with the same name are mutually exclusive.

questions.q: Method chaining in jQuery, as in $('#a').css('color','red').slideUp();, works because:
options: css() creates a new document each time
the browser compiles the calls into one statement
each jQuery method normally returns the jQuery object
slideUp() runs only after the page is closed
questions.exp: Returning the jQuery object lets the next method act on the same selection.

questions.q:
Match the HTTP status codes with their meanings:
P. 301   Q. 403   R. 503
1. Forbidden
2. Service Unavailable
3. Moved Permanently
questions.exp: 301 = Moved Permanently, 403 = Forbidden, 503 = Service Unavailable.

questions.q: The first web browser, written by Tim Berners-Lee in 1990, was named:
questions.exp: Berners-Lee's first browser/editor was called WorldWideWeb (later renamed Nexus).

questions.q: What is the specificity (ids-classes-elements) of the selector ul li.active a#link?
questions.exp: One id (#link), one class (.active) and three element names (ul, li, a) give 1-1-3.

questions.q: Why is a three-tier architecture considered more secure than a two-tier one?
options: all data is stored on the client machine
it uses HTTP instead of TCP
the database can be reached only through the application server, not directly from clients
questions.exp: In 3-tier, clients never connect to the DBMS directly, so access control and validation sit in the middle tier.
count = 3 and max = 9, so 3 + 9 = 12.

questions.q: In SOAP-based web services, WSDL is used to:
options: describe the operations, messages and endpoint of the service
questions.exp: WSDL (Web Services Description Language) is an XML description of a service's interface.

questions.q: An inverted index used by search engines maps:
options: each IP address to a domain
each URL to its file size
each term to the list of documents containing it
questions.exp: An inverted index stores, for every word, the documents (and positions) where it occurs.

questions.q: Which combination is required in an HTML form that uploads a file?
options: method="get" with the action attribute only
questions.exp: File uploads need POST and multipart/form-data so the binary content can be sent in the body.

questions.q: Which HTTP status code means "Method Not Allowed"?
questions.exp: 405 indicates the method is known but not supported for the resource.

questions.q: Which of the following is executed on the web server before the page is sent to the browser?
questions.exp: PHP is a server-side language; its output is sent to the client as HTML.

questions.q: Which JavaScript object was traditionally used by AJAX to send asynchronous HTTP requests?
questions.exp: XMLHttpRequest is the classic browser object for AJAX calls.

questions.q: In CSS, what does the selector p > span select?
options: All span elements inside any p at any depth
A span immediately following a p
Every span that is a direct child of a p
questions.exp: The child combinator '>' selects only direct children.

questions.q: After var li = document.createElement("li"); is executed, the new element:
options: is immediately visible at the end of the page
is automatically added to the first ul
exists in memory but is not in the page until it is inserted, e.g. with appendChild()
questions.exp: createElement only creates a detached node; it must be inserted into the DOM tree to appear.

questions.q: What markers does <ol type="i"> produce?
questions.exp: type="i" gives lowercase Roman numerals.

questions.q: In the URL http://example.com/page.html#section2, the part "section2" is called the:
questions.exp: The part after '#' is the fragment, which points to a location inside the page.

questions.q: The World Wide Web was proposed and developed at CERN by:
questions.exp: Tim Berners-Lee proposed the Web at CERN in 1989-90.

questions.q: Which technology defines the structure and data types of an XML document and is itself written in XML syntax?
questions.exp: XSD is an XML-based schema language; a DTD uses non-XML syntax.

questions.q: Which pair of PHP calls removes the session variables and then deletes the session?
questions.exp: session_unset() clears $_SESSION variables and session_destroy() removes the stored session data.

questions.q:
Statement I: HTTP is a stateless protocol.
Statement II: Cookies can be used by a server to maintain state across HTTP requests.
Which is correct?
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
questions.exp: HTTP does not remember earlier requests; cookies and sessions add state on top of it.

questions.q: A div has box-sizing: border-box; width: 300px; padding: 20px; border: 5px. What is its total rendered width?
questions.exp: With border-box the declared width already includes padding and border, so the total is 300px.

questions.q: A div uses the default content-box model with width: 200px; padding: 10px (all sides); border: 5px (all sides); margin: 20px. What horizontal space does the visible box (content + padding + border, excluding margin) occupy?
questions.exp: 200 + 2×10 + 2×5 = 230px; margin is outside the box.

questions.q: Which HTTP method is idempotent and is normally used to replace an existing resource completely?
questions.exp: PUT replaces the target resource with the supplied representation; repeating it gives the same result.

questions.q: Which HTTP status code indicates that a new resource has been successfully created, typically in response to a POST request?
questions.exp: 201 Created is returned when a request results in a new resource being created.

questions.q: A server returns HTTP status 401 when:
options: the request lacks valid authentication credentials
the HTTP method is not allowed
questions.exp: 401 Unauthorized means authentication is required or has failed.

questions.q: What is the default port number of the HTTPS protocol?
questions.exp: HTTPS uses TCP port 443 by default; HTTP uses 80.

questions.q: A button inside a div; both have click handlers and the event bubbles. When the button is clicked, the handlers execute in the order:
questions.exp: In the bubbling phase the event travels from the target up to its ancestors.

questions.q: What does document.getElementById("abc") return if no element has the id "abc"?
questions.exp: getElementById returns null when no matching element exists.

questions.q: In a Node.js project, which file holds the project's metadata and the list of npm dependencies?
questions.exp: npm records name, version, scripts and dependencies in package.json; installed modules go into node_modules.

questions.q: Which attribute declares a namespace in an XML document?
questions.exp: xmlns (XML namespace) associates element names with a namespace URI.

questions.q: In the MVC pattern, which component receives the user request, calls the model and selects the view to display?
questions.exp: The Controller is the intermediary: it handles input, uses the Model for data and chooses the View.

questions.q: In an XMLHttpRequest, readyState 4 together with status 200 means:
options: The request has been sent but nothing received
The request completed successfully and the response is ready
Only the headers have been received
questions.exp: readyState 4 = DONE and status 200 = OK, so the response can be used.

questions.q: In PHP, the function session_start() must be called:
options: only after the HTML body has been printed
before any output is sent to the browser, because it sends an HTTP header
questions.exp: session_start() sets the PHPSESSID cookie header, so it must come before any HTML or echo output.

questions.q: The robots.txt file on a website is used to:
options: tell crawlers which parts of the site they may or may not crawl
questions.exp: robots.txt gives crawling instructions to well-behaved web robots.

questions.q: Which jQuery method gets or sets the value of a form field such as a text box?
questions.exp: .val() works on form-element values; .text() and .html() work with element content.

questions.q: HTTPS provides confidential communication between browser and server by using:
questions.exp: HTTPS is HTTP carried over a TLS (formerly SSL) encrypted channel.

questions.q: Which HTML5 input attribute displays a short hint inside a field that disappears when the user starts typing?
questions.exp: placeholder shows greyed hint text inside an empty input.

questions.q: Which statement correctly describes the Model in the MVC pattern?
options: It renders the HTML pages shown to the user
It holds the data and business rules and is independent of the user interface
It routes browser requests to handlers
It stores only the CSS styles of the page
questions.exp: Model = data + business logic; View = presentation; Controller = request handling.

questions.q: Which technique is the most effective defence against SQL injection in PHP applications?
questions.exp: Prepared statements keep SQL code and user data separate, so input cannot change the query structure.

questions.q: The CSS rule @media (max-width: 600px) { ... } applies when:
options: the viewport width is at least 600px
the viewport width is 600px or less
the output device is a printer
questions.exp: max-width: 600px matches viewports whose width is up to and including 600px.

questions.q: Which HTTP response header instructs the browser to store a cookie?
questions.exp: The server sends Set-Cookie; the browser returns it later in the Cookie request header.

questions.q: Git is called a distributed version control system because:
options: history is stored only on one central server
every clone contains the complete repository history
it can work only over a network connection
it needs a web server to record a commit
questions.exp: Each developer has a full local repository, so commits, logs and branches work offline.

questions.q:
What is the output?
console.log("5" == 5, "5" === 5);
questions.exp: == coerces types so it is true; === also compares types so it is false.

questions.q: Which tag is essential for making a page scale properly on mobile devices in responsive design?
questions.exp: The viewport meta tag tells mobile browsers to match the device width and set initial zoom.

questions.q: Which PHP superglobal array holds the data submitted by a form that uses method="post"?
questions.exp: $_POST holds body parameters of a POST request; $_GET holds query-string parameters.

questions.q: Node.js is best described as:
options: a JavaScript runtime built on Chrome's V8 engine that runs JavaScript outside the browser
a CSS framework for responsive layouts
questions.exp: Node.js is a server-side JavaScript runtime (V8) with event-driven, non-blocking I/O; it is neither a language nor a database.

questions.q: In a two-tier client-server application, the client:
options: talks only to an intermediate application server
is always a thin browser with no logic
talks directly to the database server and usually contains the application logic
questions.exp: Two-tier = client (UI + logic, "fat client") and database server; three-tier adds a middle application tier.

questions.q: AJAX stands for:
questions.exp: AJAX = Asynchronous JavaScript and XML.

questions.q: Which PHP function opens a connection to a MySQL server using the MySQLi extension?
questions.exp: mysqli_connect(host, user, password, database) opens the connection; fetch_assoc reads a row and close ends the connection.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a valid JSON value type?
questions.exp: JSON supports object, array, string, number, boolean and null; functions are not allowed.

questions.q:
What is the output?
console.log(typeof NaN);
questions.exp: NaN is a special numeric value, so typeof NaN is "number".

questions.q: How many of seven <li> elements in a list are matched by the selector li:nth-child(odd)?
questions.exp: Positions 1, 3, 5 and 7 are odd, so 4 elements are selected.

questions.q: An HTML table has 3 rows. The first row contains a single cell with colspan="3"; each of the other two rows contains 3 cells. How many <td> elements are in the table?
questions.exp: 1 + 3 + 3 = 7 td elements.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): An element with display: none is removed from the page layout.
Reason (R): An element with visibility: hidden is also removed from the layout.
Choose the correct option.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.exp: display: none removes the element from layout, but visibility: hidden keeps the space it occupies.

questions.q: What is the result of typeof null in JavaScript?
questions.exp: typeof null returns "object"; this is a long-standing quirk of the language.

questions.q: Which attribute is used to merge a table cell across three rows?
questions.exp: rowspan makes a cell span the given number of rows; colspan spans columns.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a constraint of the REST architectural style?
questions.exp: REST requires statelessness: each request carries all needed information, so server-side session state is not part of REST.

questions.q: In a typical three-tier web application where PHP scripts run on an Apache server and data is kept in MySQL, the PHP scripts form the:
questions.exp: Browser = presentation tier, web/application server running PHP = logic tier, MySQL = data tier.

questions.q: Two vertically adjacent block siblings have margin-bottom: 30px on the first and margin-top: 20px on the second. What is the gap between them due to margin collapsing?
questions.exp: Adjoining vertical margins collapse to the larger of the two, i.e. 30px.

questions.q: What does document.querySelector(".box") return?
options: A live HTMLCollection of all matches
The first element matching the selector
questions.exp: querySelector returns only the first matching element (or null); querySelectorAll returns a NodeList.

questions.q: In a RESTful API, which request is the most appropriate way to delete the user with id 5?
questions.exp: REST maps the delete operation to the DELETE method on the resource URI.

questions.q:
In jQuery, which statement hides every

element on the page?
questions.exp: Syntax is $(selector).action(); "p" is an element selector, ".p" a class selector and "#p" an id selector.

questions.q: Which of the following is a valid JSON object?
questions.exp: JSON requires double-quoted keys and strings and does not allow trailing commas.

questions.q: Which value of the CSS position property positions an element relative to the browser viewport and keeps it in place while scrolling?
questions.exp: position: fixed is positioned relative to the viewport and does not move on scroll.

questions.q: The fetch() function of the browser returns:
questions.exp: fetch() returns a Promise that resolves to a Response object.
Setting length to 1 truncates the array to its first element.

questions.q:
Statement I: REST is an architectural style rather than a protocol.
Statement II: SOAP messages can be transported only over HTTP.
Which is correct?
questions.exp: SOAP is protocol-independent and can run over SMTP, TCP etc., so Statement II is false.

questions.q: A well-formed XML document must have:
questions.exp: Well-formedness requires a single root element, properly nested and closed tags.

questions.q: When a form is submitted with method="GET", the form data is:
options: sent only in the request body
appended to the URL as a query string
questions.exp: GET appends name=value pairs to the URL after '?'.
